data.title: Primary Key
data.tagline: The field in a table used to uniquely identify each row
data.learningOutcome: Given a table, you can point to the column that uniquely identifies a row and explain why the others cannot.
data.description: If two rows in a users table share an email, an update by email matches both; an update limited to primary key id = 7 identifies the target row. Check the matching count before writing and read the table again to confirm the other row stayed unchanged. A primary key can be one column or a group, and its value is unique and non-null.

learning.assumes: You have seen table data, or AI mentioning updating a record by id.
learning.outcome: Given a table, you can point to the column that uniquely identifies a row and explain why the others cannot.

distinctions.label: Index
distinctions.explanation: An index is a structure that speeds up lookups and does not guarantee uniqueness; a primary key guarantees uniqueness and usually has an index.

distinctions.label: Ordinary field
distinctions.explanation: Fields like name and email can contain duplicates; a primary key's values cannot repeat and cannot be empty.

explanation.title: Locate one row, not a batch
explanation.text: A primary key uniquely identifies a row; still inspect the write condition, affected-row count, and read-back result. A repeated field can match multiple rows.

explanation.title: Ordinary fields repeat
explanation.text: Identical names and emails happen all the time; a primary key's values cannot repeat and cannot be empty.

explanation.title: Tables link through it
explanation.text: When an orders table records which user an order belongs to, it stores the users table's primary key, not the name.

data.boundary: A primary key guarantees uniqueness, not correctness. When two rows look duplicated, find out why first—duplicate entry or a migration error—rather than deleting one.

lessonPractice.title: You want to update someone's profile by email in a user table that has two identical emails. What is the problem?

options.label: This table has repeated emails; use its defined primary key id to identify the target row
options.feedback: Correct. Emails repeat in this table, so an email condition matches multiple rows; id is this table's designated primary key and identifies the target row.

options.label: Update any one of the rows; the impact is small
options.feedback: Editing the wrong row edits someone else's data; location must be unique.

options.label: Delete all duplicate-email records first and keep one
options.feedback: Deleting data is dangerous; find out why duplicates exist and decide to merge or fix, not delete.

data.agentPrompt: Update this user record by primary key, not by email or name. Before updating, tell me how many rows match; if more than one, stop and explain before continuing. After the change, query the record again to confirm.
